newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia's prosecutor appeals Salus decision.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia's prosecutor appeals Salus decision.

text.p: Slovenia's state prosecutor said on Thursday he had appealed against a decision by the Ljubljana district court that pharmaceutical wholesaler Salus would not have to change its ownership structure.
"We still insist that Salus's 1990 privatisation process was incorrect and has to be changed, that is why we have appealed," Janez Krnc, deputy state prosecutor, told Reuters.
Salus shares have risen 14.5 percent since August 27, when the district court found Salus not guilty of a faulty privatisation process.
"We expect the higher court to annul the decision of the district court," Krnc said.

In February, Salus appealed against a decision by the Slovenian Payment Agency ordering it to introduce an 80-percent state stake in the company. The agency said Salus, which was formerly state-owned, incorrectly transferred state capital to its newly established subsidiary Finsa in 1991.
"As experience shows, the proceeding could last up to one year," Krnc added.
